title: Alien Winds
summary: Slow, breathing gusts made from filtered noise, with the LFO shaping motion and the Brain adding an unpredictable pulse pattern.

settings: X/Y/Z are upper knobs left to right; A/B are lower buttons. Press A to run.
X: 100% tempo. Y: 100% octave range. Z: 100% randomness.
PULSE modulates Filter CV1. The random pattern can occasionally slow to zero and let the wind die away.

sound: A low, resonant wind bed rises and falls in long gusts. Filter movement gives the noise a distant, otherworldly voice rather than a steady hiss.
setup: Remove existing patch cables. Make the six numbered instrument connections. The dashed ENV OUT to CONTROL path is internal; the headphone lead is separate.
Use VCO 2's NOISE output. Connect stereo headphones to the final output and begin with output volume at minimum.
The percentages are physical starting positions. Adjust by ear for differences in analog timing, filter response, and VCA calibration.
Set the marked controls, select Sequencer mode, power on, then raise output volume slowly and press A. The right envelope LED, LFO LED, and Brain A LED should pulse.
play: Turn filter cutoff slowly to search for vocal and whistling bands.
Use LFO rate as the main performance control. Very slow settings make broad gusts; faster settings produce rhythmic breathing.
At full Brain randomness the pattern occasionally slows to zero and dies away. Press A if the sequencer has stopped; otherwise let the silence resolve into the next gust.
variations: CV1 and CV2 both modulate cutoff. Use either or both; each LEVEL sets depth and reverses direction around center.
LFO TRI gives a smooth sweep, Brain PULSE gives short accents, and Brain OUT/1 gives stepped changes held between sequencer steps.

Pairs: TRI + PULSE adds accents to smooth gusts; TRI + OUT/1 mixes smooth and stepped motion; PULSE + OUT/1 makes an abrupt sequenced storm. A splitter or stackable cable can send one source to both inputs; align LEVELs to reinforce it or oppose them to partly cancel.
Sweep resonance from 60% to 100% to move from broad wind to a narrow, singing whistle. Lower output volume if it becomes piercing.

normalled_policy: ENV/VCA 2 ENV OUT -> CONTROL remains internally normalled (N1), saving one patch cable. Physical cables override both filter CV inputs and the filter audio input; the left Envelope/VCA and all other default paths are excluded from the output.

vco2.wave.irrelevant: The dedicated NOISE output is used; the main oscillator waveform is not in the audio path.

vco2.octave.irrelevant: The dedicated NOISE output is independent of oscillator tuning.

vco2.fine.irrelevant: The dedicated NOISE output is independent of oscillator tuning.

vco2.width.irrelevant: The square-wave output is not used.
